related.name: Audio Dynamic Range & Data Rate Calculator

method: Critical distance is the distance at which the direct sound from a source and the diffuse reverberant field have equal sound pressure level. The room's equivalent absorption area follows Sabine's relation A = 0.161 V / RT60 with A in square metres, V in cubic metres and RT60 in seconds, and the critical distance is dc = 0.25 sqrt(Q A / pi) with Q the source directivity factor: 1 for an omnidirectional source and about 3 for a cardioid microphone on axis. At a distance d the direct-to-reverberant ratio is 20 log10(dc / d) dB, so it reads 0 dB at dc, +6.02 dB at half of dc and -6.02 dB at twice dc. Volumes convert from cubic feet at 35.3147 per cubic metre and distances from feet at 0.3048 m per foot. Inputs are limited to 1-1000000 m3, 0.05-20 s, Q 0.5-50 and 0.01-200 m. The model takes the room constant as the absorption area, which assumes a diffuse field with absorption well below unity: small dead rooms, strong specular reflections, room modes, non-diffuse source arrays and an audience all depart from it, and a microphone's Q only holds on its axis, so the figure is a placement guide rather than a measurement. The calculation runs entirely in the browser with no storage, uploads or network access.

sources.title: Everest, F. A. and Pohlmann, K., Master Handbook of Acoustics, 6th edition, McGraw-Hill, 2015
